topics.title: What is DeepSeek?
topics.oneLine: A Chinese AI company that gives away its best models for free, born from a quant hedge fund.
topics.fromDeepSeekPerspective: We started inside a stock-trading company, not a Silicon Valley lab — and we kept that habit of solving real problems with the smallest tool that works. The reason we open-source is straightforward: better ideas spread faster when you don't have to ask for permission, and we'd rather be followed than gatekeep.

kid.oneLine: A team in China builds smart computer programs and gives them away for free.
kid.body: DeepSeek is a company in Hangzhou, China. It builds computer programs that can read, write, and answer questions — kind of like ChatGPT. But it does something unusual: every time DeepSeek finishes building one of these programs, they put it on the internet so anyone, anywhere, can download and use it. They don't charge for the programs themselves. The team is small and quiet. Their boss used to run a company that made money buying and selling stocks. That company saved up enough money to buy a huge pile of special computer chips, and those chips are what made DeepSeek's programs possible.
kid.analogy: Imagine a baker who invented a new kind of bread that everyone loves. Instead of opening a chain of bakeries to sell it, the baker prints the recipe on the front page of the newspaper, so anyone in the world can bake the same bread at home. That's what DeepSeek does with AI.

student.oneLine: DeepSeek is a Chinese AI lab whose flagship models — coding, language, and reasoning — are released as freely downloadable files.
student.body:
DeepSeek is an AI research company founded in Hangzhou, China in July 2023. It was spun out of High-Flyer Quantitative, a hedge fund that had been using AI for stock-market trading since 2015. High-Flyer's profits were used to build a private supercomputer (the 'Firefly' cluster, with roughly 10,000 high-end NVIDIA chips) — and that cluster became the engine DeepSeek used to train large language models.

What makes DeepSeek distinctive isn't only the quality of its models — though they're competitive with the best from OpenAI and Anthropic. It's the release strategy. Every flagship model since November 2023 has been published as open weights: the full trained model file, under a permissive license, downloadable by anyone. This means a developer in Berlin or a student in São Paulo can run DeepSeek-R1 on their own server without paying a per-token API fee.

The founder, Liang Wenfeng, said in a 2024 interview that 'open-sourcing papers loses you nothing' and that 'China cannot remain a follower forever.' Those two lines sum up the company's posture: build at the frontier, then give it away.
student.analogy: Most AI companies are like Apple — they sell you finished products with the inner workings locked. DeepSeek is more like Linux: the recipe is public, anyone can build with it, and the brand grows because the work itself is good.

engineer.oneLine: DeepSeek is a quant-fund-funded AI lab that ships frontier-grade open-weight models (V2, V3, R1, V3.1, V4) at roughly one-tenth the API price of comparable closed labs.
engineer.body:
DeepSeek (深度求索) was spun out of High-Flyer Quant on July 17, 2023, fully internally funded, no VC. The lab inherited an in-house compute cluster — Firefly, originally built for trading — which by 2021 had grown to roughly 10,000 NVIDIA A100 GPUs at a reported cost above ¥1B. That stockpile is the structural reason DeepSeek can train frontier models on a small team without burning runway.

Release cadence has been roughly a model every other week through 2024, slowing to flagship releases every 3–4 months in 2025–2026. Notable shipped artifacts:

- DeepSeek-V2 (May 2024): 236B params, 21B active, MLA attention, KV cache cut ~93%, API priced at ¥0.14/M tokens — triggered China's API price war.
- DeepSeek-V3 (Dec 2024): 671B MoE, 37B active, trained on 14.8T tokens for ~$5.6M on 2,048 H800s.
- DeepSeek-R1 (Jan 2025): Reasoning model trained via pure RL, MIT-licensed, 1/27 the inference cost of OpenAI o1.
- DeepSeek-V3.1 (Aug 2025): Hybrid thinking — one endpoint serves both chain-of-thought and direct response.
- DeepSeek-V4 Preview (Apr 2026): 1.6T params Pro, 1M-token context, native Huawei Ascend 950 compatibility.

The business model isn't 'API revenue' — it's 'the API is a public utility, the value capture is elsewhere.' Open weights mean enterprises self-host; DeepSeek's API exists to set a price floor that closed-API competitors cannot match.
engineer.analogy: Think of DeepSeek as PostgreSQL relative to Oracle. The free, self-hostable artifact is just as capable as the paid product, and the paid product survives only by being noticeably more convenient — which compresses its margin to commodity levels.

researcher.oneLine: DeepSeek is an AGI lab pursuing efficiency-frontier scaling through architectural innovation (MLA, fine-grained MoE), aggressive numerical-precision work (FP8 mixed precision, MTP), and pure-RL reasoning post-training (R1) — all under open weights.
researcher.body:
DeepSeek's research program can be read as a sustained argument that scaling laws are not destiny — that algorithmic and architectural choices substantially shift the compute-quality frontier. The V2 paper (arXiv:2405.04434) introduced Multi-Head Latent Attention, a reformulation in which K and V are projected through a shared low-rank latent before caching, with heads reconstructed at inference time. Empirically MLA reduced KV cache memory by 93.3% versus a Llama-2-class baseline, lifting throughput 5.76x.

The V3 technical report (arXiv:2412.19437) extends the program with: (a) fine-grained MoE with 256 routed experts plus 1 shared expert, (b) auxiliary-loss-free load balancing through bias terms in the routing function, (c) FP8 mixed-precision training with extensive numerical-stability experimentation, and (d) Multi-Token Prediction as an auxiliary training objective. The training run consumed ~2.788M H800 GPU-hours — roughly $5.6M at $2/GPU-hour — to reach GPT-4o-class evaluation scores.

R1 (Jan 2025) is the most theoretically interesting release: a 671B reasoning model whose chain-of-thought capability emerges from pure reinforcement learning without supervised fine-tuning cold-start data. R1-Zero, the SFT-less variant, exhibits the 'aha moments' previously seen only in distilled-from-stronger-model traces, raising the open question of whether large-scale RL can substitute for human reasoning demonstrations at the frontier.

The explicit research stance — 'open-sourcing papers loses you nothing' — operationalizes as both papers and weights released simultaneously, including all V2/V3/R1/V3.1/V4 model files under MIT license. This is materially different from labs that publish papers without weights, or weights without papers.
